newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate pares advance at close on FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate pares advance at close on FOMC.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates receded from earlier increases to close up just 20 basis points at 18.40 percent on Tuesday on news the Federal Open Market Comittee decided not to raise U.S. base rates, traders said.
"Rates receded a little after the FOMC announcement, it didn't plunge as it has done, down to 17 percent," a trader said.
The FOMC stated with about two hours of dealing left it would leave the U.S. federal funds rate at 5.50 percent, and the discount rate at 5.0 percent.
The dealer said an excess of paper in the system due to central bank intervention helped to cushion the late fall in secondary rates.
"The market felt heavily loaded with paper at the close, that is why rates did not decline more," he said.
Banco de Mexico drained 6.936 billion pesos by three direct Cetes sales combined with eight repos.

Traders said the FOMC news came after the central bank had closed bidding for its weekly primary auction of government securities, and was not therefore expected to influence the results, due at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
A Reuters survey nN20539678 revealed traders forecast bellwether 28-day Cetes would fall by an average of 11 basis points to 18.80 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile declined 20 basis points to 19.30 percent.
June Cetes futures traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange gained 28 centavos to 78.80 pesos.
Liquidity of 236 million pesos was due to flow back into the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
